title: Leadership & mentoring signals
exp: At 4 YOE, you're expected to multiply the team's output, not just your own. Prepare two short STAR stories before any interview.
pts: **Code review philosophy:** correctness, readability, test coverage, consistency with existing patterns, performance — give specific feedback with examples, not vague critique
**Constructive pushback:** describe a time you disagreed with a technical decision, how you raised it with data/reasoning (not emotion), and the outcome
**Mentoring:** even informal counts — explaining N+1 to a colleague, teaching comments in a PR, pairing on a tricky edge case
**Two STAR stories to prepare:** (1) technical disagreement/pushback, (2) helping a teammate grow

viz.note: Run a mock behavioral round with your AI: "Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision." Then critique your own STAR structure.

qa.q: How do you approach a code review when you find significant issues?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** I prioritise by impact: blocking (correctness, security, data loss) vs non-blocking (style, minor improvements). For blocking issues I explain specifically what could go wrong, not just flag it. For non-blocking improvements I prefix with "optional:" so the author knows what's required vs suggested. I also note what's good in the PR — positive feedback helps people understand what "good" looks like.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** EF Core builds an Expression Tree, translates it via the relational SQL provider into a parameterized T-SQL query, and materializes entities into the DbContext Change Tracker. N+1 queries occur when navigating un-included navigation properties in a loop.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing queries without AsNoTracking() in read-only APIs forces EF Core to keep snapshot copies of all returned entities in memory, causing high RAM usage and CPU tracking overhead.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** AsNoTracking() speeds up read queries by 20-30% and reduces memory footprint, but disables identity resolution and automatic change tracking for updates.

qa.q: Tell me about a time you pushed back on a technical decision.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** (Prepare a real story.) Frame it as: the decision, why you disagreed, how you raised it constructively with data/reasoning, the outcome, and what you'd do the same or differently. Interviewers are testing that you can disagree professionally — not that you're contrarian.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: How would you handle a junior developer who keeps submitting code below team standards?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** First understand why: knowledge gap, unclear standards, or time pressure? If knowledge gap: pair program, show specifically what good looks like. If standards are unclear: advocate for documented standards or linter rules. If time pressure causing shortcuts: that's a planning conversation, not a dev conversation. Escalate only if the pattern continues after active support.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** SQL Server compiles T-SQL into an execution plan based on statistics histogram estimates. Parameter sniffing occurs when a plan compiled for a specific parameter (e.g. 1 row) is reused for a parameter matching 1,000,000 rows, leading to index scan or memory grant spills.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Implicit datatype conversion (e.g. passing NVARCHAR parameter to VARCHAR indexed column) forces SQL Server to run CONVERT() on every row, turning index seeks into full index scans.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT (RCSI) eliminates reader-writer blocking using tempdb row versioning, but increases tempdb I/O and version store management overhead.
